items.title: Murmur: Efficient Long-Context ASR Inference with Hierarchical Chunking
items.summary_1line: Murmur: Efficient Long-Context ASR Inference with Hierarchical Chunking
items.editor_note: Newest: carries the efficiency theme to speech, with hierarchical chunking for long-context ASR inference.

editorial.tldr: This is a loose cluster of independent inference-efficiency work, not one event. It opened Oct 30 with pruning, MoE quantization and prompt compression, added block-diffusion decoding papers Nov 8-10, then shifted to vendor posts and agent-side token spend by Nov 15-17.
editorial.whats_new: A University of Washington post (Nov 18) introduces Murmur, which uses hierarchical chunking to speed long-context speech recognition inference, a day after a paper that compresses activations to cut MoE expert-parallel communication.
editorial.why_it_matters: Inference cost is now attacked at every layer at once: model weights, MoE communication, decoding, prompts, agent token spend, and non-text workloads like long audio.
editorial.take_for_builders: Log tokens per completed agent task and GPU-seconds per audio hour before adopting any of these methods, so each claimed saving can be measured against your own baseline; do not plan capacity around diffusion LLMs yet.

beats.headline: Pruning, MoE quantization and input compression shrink inference cost
beats.summary: Five papers cut cost on the model or input side: extreme-sparsity pruning, Matryoshka MoE with mixed precision, RL-trained prompt compression, VLM image cropping, and compressed activations for MoE expert parallelism.

beats.headline: Block-diffusion work targets draft-tree verification and block-boundary latency
beats.summary: D3Tree prunes block-diffusion draft trees for speculative decoding, and overlapping block denoising cuts latency in block diffusion LMs.

beats.headline: Agent papers attack prompt-carried skill memory and wasted delegation
beats.summary: MDSKILL distills skill memory into weights instead of prompts; a deep-research paper argues delegation only pays off when allocation and execution are coordinated.

beats.headline: Efficiency reaches vendors, agent products and speech: Baseten, Nemotron Bolt, TokenEconomizer, Murmur
beats.summary: The latest items are blog posts and a shipped small model rather than arXiv method papers, now extending to long-context ASR.

open_questions: How much does TokenEconomizer cut tokens per resolved coding task, and on which agent harness and benchmark?
Does Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B hold tool-calling accuracy at 4GB against Gemma-4-E4B-it, the model it was post-trained from?
Does activation compression for expert parallelism hold model quality while cutting all-to-all traffic in a production MoE serving stack?
Does Murmur's hierarchical chunking keep transcript accuracy on hour-long audio compared with full-context decoding?
Does any inference framework or vendor ship diffusion LLM serving with parallel decoding?
Do the pruning and MoE quantization gains hold on agentic and long-context tasks, not only perplexity and short benchmarks?
